desc:
prices[i] is the price of a stock on day i (days are numbered from 0). You make a single trade: buy on day b and sell on a later day s > b.

Return [b, s] for the trade with the largest profit. If several trades have the same maximum profit, take the one with the smallest sell day, and among those the smallest buy day. If no trade has a positive profit, return [-1, -1].

Example: prices = [7,1,5,3,6,4] gives [1, 4] (buy at 1, sell at 6, profit 5).
hints: For a fixed sell day, which buy day is best?
The best buy day for a sell day is the day with the lowest price before it. Scan left to right and remember that day.

Keep the index of the lowest price so far (replace it only on a strictly lower price so the earliest wins). For each day compute the profit against it and replace the answer only on a strictly larger profit, so the earliest sell day wins.
editorial: For a sell day s the best buy day is the earliest day before s with the minimum price. Maintain lo, the index of the lowest price seen so far, updating it only when a strictly smaller price appears. This yields the earliest minimum for ties.

At each day compute prices[s] - prices[lo]. If it is strictly larger than the best profit so far (which starts at 0), store [lo, s]. Because the scan moves forward and the update needs a strictly larger profit, among equal maxima the first one found has the smallest sell day, exactly as the statement requires.
A single pass: O(n) time and O(1) space. Comparing all pairs would be O(n^2).
